enso.cpc_discussion: ENSO Alert System Status: El Niño Advisory   Synopsis:   El Niño continues to strengthen, with a strong-to-very strong El Niño likely through January-March 2027 (remaining greater than an 83% chance). El Niño strengthened further last month, with sea surface temperature anomalies exceeding +4.0°C in portions of the eastern equatorial Pacific [Fig. 1] . Most Niño indices increased in the past month, reaching +2.1°C in Niño-3.4, +3.0°C in Niño-3, and +3.9°C in Niño-1+2 [Fig. 2] . The equatorial subsurface temperature index (average from 180°-100°W) was well above average [Fig. 3] , reflecting a deeper-than-average thermocline. Subsurface temperatures remained in excess of +10.0°C at depth in the eastern Pacific Ocean [Fig. 4] . Low-level westerly wind anomalies and upper-level easterly wind anomalies stretched from the western to the east-central equatorial Pacific. Enhanced convection and rainfall persisted from the central to the eastern Pacific, while anomalies remained suppressed over Indonesia [Fig. 5] . The traditional and equatorial Southern Oscillation indices were significantly negative. Collectively, the coupled ocean-atmosphere system reflected a strengthening El Niño. The CPC Official ENSO outlook , which synthesizes multiple models from North America and abroad, indicates El Niño will continue to strengthen through the end of the year [Figs. 6 -7 -8] . notes: Wind/gust ranges: quantile-boosted models widened by a conformal margin fit on out-of-fold errors (days 1-10 ensemble model).

Temperature ranges: NBM high/low plus the empirical error distribution (by lead day and season) measured at Alamogordo, Holloman and Las Cruces airports; the same error spread is assumed at Hawk St, the Pass and Cloudcroft (mountain sites are not verified).
Rain: percentile amounts come from the hurdle model; coverage above nominal mostly reflects the large share of dry days. Cloudcroft days 8-10 slightly under-cover (88% vs 90%).
Test period: Jul 2025 – Oct 2026 (about 15 months), so coverage numbers carry a few points of sampling noise.

National Weather Service El Paso TX/Santa Teresa NM
513 PM MST Fri Nov 13 2026

...New AVIATION...

.KEY MESSAGES... 
Updated at 445 PM MST Fri Nov 13 2026

 - A Pacific cold front and upper level system will bring rain
   showers and isolated thunderstorms to the area this afternoon
   and evening. A few bands of heavier rain will be possible, 
   especially across West Texas.

 - Breezy and cooler on Saturday, with lowland highs in the lower
   60s. Isolated to widely scattered rain and snow showers will
   affect the Sacramento Mountains and parts of the Gila On
   Saturday afternoon. 

 - Temperatures look to remain slightly below normal into next
   week.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
Issued at 1126 AM MST Fri Nov 13 2026

A sharp upper level trough over Arizona is moving steadily to the
east. Thunderstorms are common across southern Arizona into
northern Sonora, ahead of the main vort max moving across the
northern Gulf of California. Diffluent flow over southern New
Mexico and a weak shortwave trough has lead to increasing
convective shower coverage over south-central New Mexico, and more
recently around El Paso. This activity is expected to intensify 
as it spreads northeast through the afternoon hours.

Near-term models have been fairly inconsistent with the details
through the evening and overnight hours. It seems the current
precip will be the main wave of precip, with a secondary area of
showers and thunderstorms possibly moving into southern Dona Ana
and El Paso Counties closer to sunset. Activity over Arizona looks
to become weaker and more scattered as it shifts into southern New
Mexico overnight, with some CAMS really inhibiting precip coverage
later tonight. But, it seems wise to hold onto shower chances as
long as the main trough axis is to our west. Also, the GFS has
most of the area in the left exit region of a 100+ knot jet streak
overnight, further favoring rain chances.

Some small hail could accompany stronger embedded thunderstorms
this afternoon and evening, particularly over Otero and Hudspeth
Counties.

Snow levels will drop to around 9500-10,000 feet overnight, with
light snow accumulations possible in the highest elevations of 
Sacramento Mountains, though mostly around uninhabited high peaks. 

A northern stream shortwave trough will roll across northern New
Mexico on Saturday. Continued cyclonic flow and cooler air aloft
will promote increasing cloud cover and convective shower chances
over northern sections of the CWA Saturday afternoon. Scattered
rain and "graupelly" snow showers will be possible over the
Sacramento Mountains and the Black Range around mid to late 
afternoon, though no accumulation is expected. Elsewhere, expect
breezy west winds across the lowlands, with some gusts around 35
mph at times. 

Lighter NW winds will prevail on Sunday, with more sunshine, no
showers, and temperatures remaining about 3 to 6 degrees below 
normal.

&&

.AVIATION...
(00Z TAFS)
Issued at 445 PM MST Fri Nov 13 2026

We have an active weather pattern over the next 24 hours. A line
of thunderstorms is moving across the area. The line has already
cleared all the TAF sites and the line will continue to push to
the east at 15 to 20 mph. It does seem likely that we will see 
another round or two of showers and thunderstorms this evening 
through about 2 AM. The thunderstorms and showers may give us 
brief MVFR visibilities, but ceilings are expected to remain VFR. 
By 3 AM most of the convection will be east of the area. The 
clouds will linger through the day on Saturday, so we will 
continue to have high ceilings of BKN120. By early afternoon our
surface winds will also increase from the west and be gusty from 
time to time; 26015G25KT.

&&

.FIRE WEATHER...
Issued at 150 PM MST Fri Nov 13 2026

Low fire weather concerns continue as ERCs remain low, and RH values
are high. Showers and isolated thunderstorms to day into tonight will
keep that trend going. Breezy conditions, with west winds gusting to
35 mph at times in the afternoon Saturday, will be of little concern
given ongoing moist conditions and below normal temperatures. Some
rain/snow showers are possible Saturday afternoon in the Black Range 
and Sacramento Mountains. 

&&
